commentary.title: Men's Norman Eastwood - Comedy Recap
commentary.overallSummary: Fifteen men went out, eighteen holes were played, and several of them should honestly not be believed when they claim golf is a hobby they're good at. Adam ran away with it while everyone else spent the day rediscovering exactly how little control they have over a small white ball. Blobs were dished out like parking tickets, back nines were treated as optional extras, and at least four grown men needed reminding that the ball is meant to travel forward. Throw in a league leader having a shocker and the club's worst-placed player quietly posting his best round of the year, and this was a genuinely chaotic day out for the collective ego.

playerCommentary.summary: Adam blitzed the field for the win with 48 points, comfortably his best haul of the season and a good ten points clear of his usual average of 38.12, so evidently he saves the good stuff for competitions with 'Trophy' in the title. He was tidy on the front nine (18) and even better coming home (20), driven by a scarcely believable eagle-class 4 on the 8th and more good work at 10, 13, 14 and 16. Somewhere in the middle of all that brilliance he still found room for a blob on the 3rd, presumably just to remind everyone he's human.

Marc's 44 points made this comfortably his best outing of the season, nearly eight points clear of his 36.38 average, built almost entirely on a phenomenal front nine of 22 with big scores at 1, 5, 6, 7 and 8. Then the back nine happened - a miserable 14, complete with matching blobs at the 10th and 13th, as if his ball filed for a transfer the second he made the turn. Somewhere out there is a version of Marc who plays the back nine like the front and wins this thing outright.

Colin's near-mirror-image round - 17 on the front, 17 on the back, decent scores scattered at 1, 7, 11, 14 and 16 - would have been genuinely elite if not for a single infuriating blob on the 12th that likely cost him a real shot at the title. Third place and 40 points is still a tidy day's work, sitting comfortably above his season average of 37.88, but he'll know that 12th hole owes him one.

Simon fell flat on his face out of the gate with blobs on both the 1st and 2nd, the golfing equivalent of tripping over your own shoelaces before the starting gun's even fired. Somehow he then produced a stellar back nine of 19 points, including strong scoring at 11, 12 and 13, to finish with 38 - comfortably one of his best rounds of the season against a 32.5 average, and proof that his season-long form has been criminally undersold.

Thomas turned in a genuinely strong back nine of 18 points, powered by good scoring at 12, 13 and 14, more than making up for a front nine ruined by matching blobs at the 8th and 11th that bookended the turn like a pair of unwelcome guests. His 35 points sit nicely above his 32.62 season average, so this was actually a good day at the office for a man usually lurking mid-table.

Craig produced the only completely blob-free card in the entire field, with tidy scoring at 5 and 7 the closest thing to a highlight. But 'consistent' and 'competitive' aren't the same thing here - his 33 points is a good six and a half shy of his season average of 39.62, for a man currently sitting third overall. No drama, no disasters, and not much to write home about beyond the fact he didn't actively embarrass himself.

Lee's front nine of 19 points, nearly all 2s and a lone 3 at the 5th, looked like the round of his life in the making. Then the course remembered who he was and served up blobs at 13 and 17 to drag him back to a fairly pedestrian 33, a touch under his 35.5 season average and a timely reminder that golf enjoys nothing more than punishing hope.

Mark blobbed four holes on the front nine alone - literally half of it, at 1, 2, 7 and 8 - for a woeful 13, before an entirely different golfer turned up for the back nine with a superb 20, including big scores at the 5th, 12th, 14th and 16th. The 33-point total is, remarkably, his best round of the season by some distance against a 26.83 average, so bottom of the overall standings has never looked more like an accident.

Joseph was cruising toward a genuinely tidy card - 17 out, 15 back, with useful scoring at 1, 7 and 12 - until an inexplicable blob on the 17th spoiled what should have been a clean sweep. His 32 points is a shade under his season average of 36.75, so file this one under 'nearly, but not quite,' with the 17th hole as the culprit.

Neil currently tops the entire season standings with a 43.0 average, which makes this 32-point return a genuinely poor day at the office relative to his usual standard. A solid front nine of 18, featuring good scoring at 1, 4, 5 and 12, was undone by a back nine that limped to 14 and included a blob on the 16th. The man leading the whole competition just had one of his worst rounds of the year, and somewhere his nearest rivals will be smiling.

Stephen's front nine was a genuine mess - 14 points including a blob at the 4th sandwiched around a brilliant 4 on the 5th, like a man arguing with himself hole by hole. The back nine (18), with more good scoring at 11 and 12, was far better, but a second blob at the 13th did enough damage that his overall 32 sits well below his 37.88 season average.

Graham sits second in the entire season standings with a 41.38 average, which makes today's flat, blob-marred 30 - 15 out, 15 back, with a single decent score at the 5th and a zero on the 8th - look like a genuine off day for a man who's usually near the top of every leaderboard. Perfectly symmetrical golf, but symmetrically underwhelming.

Terry's card reads like a fever dream - two brilliant scores on the 5th and 15th surrounded by four separate blobs at 9, 11, 16 and 17, the sort of round that gives your playing partners whiplash. Somehow the 30 points is still marginally above his 28.75 season average, so for a man second from bottom in the overall standings, this chaos actually counts as progress.

Paul opened with a blob on the very first hole, the golfing equivalent of falling flat on your face in front of the whole clubhouse, then added three more at 11, 12 and 15 for good measure, rescued only by decent scoring at 7, 8, 14 and 17. His 30 points is a full six shy of his 36.0 season average, which tells you this was very much not his day.

James brought up the rear with 25 points, propped up only by decent scores at 3, 10 and 12, but undone by four separate blobs including a truly grim finish at 17 and 18. Even against his own modest season average of 30.43, this was a below-par effort in every sense, and the sort of card best forgotten quickly.
